review.reason:
Candidate 5 passes as supplied, with no geometry edits needed.

Hole 1 is a dry 206-yard par 3 with a clear, playable target and limited greenside bunkering. It offers a straightforward distance-control test, appropriately distinct from the longer route-choice holes.

Hole 2 is a 490-yard dogleg-right par 5 with one substantial water hazard along the side of play. The broad landing area and 70 safe tee options support a staged route, while the bend and shoreline make an aggressive advance a meaningful risk-reward choice. The simulated two-shot reach is evidence of an opportunity, not a guarantee.

Hole 3 is a dry 400-yard double-dogleg par 4. Its bends and fairway bunker give placement choices substance, while the available corridor and 47 safe tee options indicate a playable line. Greenside bunkers add approach consequences without closing off the target.

The par-3/5/4 sequence, one substantial lake, and contrasting straight, bending, and double-bending layouts provide excellent within-round variety. Recent rounds include dry long par 3s and double-dogleg par 4s, so novelty is good rather than exceptional; the wet dogleg-right par 5 and this combination and sequence keep the round sufficiently distinct. The safe-option counts and simulated shots-to-green support fair difficulty, and the numbered previews show credible landing space and targets.
